items.description: it's insane what you can make with Seedance 2.5 just made this entire video from a single prompt, no camera, no editing, nothing if you want to make videos like this, check my free guide below full prompt for this video:
items.prompt: it's insane what you can make with Seedance 2.5 just made this entire video from a single prompt, no camera, no editing, nothing if you want to make videos like this, check my free guide below full prompt for this video: CAMERA: Handheld DV 16mm daily vlog footage. The video MUST begin with her propping the camera against a jar of flour on the kitchen counter, shooting her from a three-quarter angle as she cooks. She picks it up for close-ups of the food, then sets it back. The camera gets flour dust on the lens at one point — she wipes it with her sleeve and keeps going. Keep subtle handheld shake, drifting composition, autofocus hunting, rushed reframing when something sizzles, exposure breathing between the dark counter and the bright stove, and imperfect framing throughout. The camera itself is never visible. LOOK: Warm kitchen lighting — a single overhead fixture casting yellowish light, the stove adding a bright warm glow on the food. Steam and smoke catch the light. Gentle film grain heavy in the shadows, slightly softened sharpness, subtle halation from the stove flame. Her face is warm and golden. It should feel like authentic footage from someone's everyday life rather than a polished commercial. STYLE: A comfortable, slightly chaotic cooking vlog. She talks to the camera like a friend is in the room. Small laughs, pauses, fixing her hair, wiping her hands on the apron, tasting and reacting. She makes small mistakes and laughs at herself. She speaks in short, natural sentences with frequent pauses. Never rush dialogue. Leave quiet moments between lines. CHARACTER: A beautiful woman in her late 20s. Long dark brown hair tied back in a low messy bun with a kitchen towel over her shoulder, warm olive skin, brown eyes, no makeup. She wears a cream-colored linen shirt with the sleeves rolled up and a dark green apron. Flour on her cheek. Natural, relaxed, a little messy. SETTING: A small home kitchen in the evening. White tile counter, a gas stove with a well-used pan, a cutting board with onions and garlic, a jar of flour, a wooden spoon, a glass of red wine. The overhead light is the only source. A window above the sink shows darkness outside. Intimate and slightly cluttered. SCENES: The vlog opens with the camera propped against a flour jar. She chops an onion, eyes watering. "I don't know why I keep doing this to myself." She wipes her eye with the back of her wrist. Picks up the camera, holds it close to the cutting board. "Look. The onion won." Sets it back. Pours olive oil into the pan. It sizzles loud. She jumps. She adds the onion. Steam rises into the light. She stirs. "Okay that smells better." She sips from a glass of wine. Looks at the camera. "Don't judge." She adds garlic. It sizzles harder. She moves the pan off the heat. "Too hot. Always too hot." She picks up the camera, selfie mode, flour on her cheek. She hasn't noticed. "It's going to be fine. Probably." She tastes from the wooden spoon, winces, then nods. "Okay. Yeah. It's good." Flour dust on the lens. She wipes it with her sleeve. A smile. The frame goes dark. Cut.

items.description: A FILM PRODUCER BLOCKED ME MID-CONVERSATION OVER THIS SEEDANCE 2.0 CLIP I posted it privately in a group chat. He DM’d one question: “How much did this cost?” I told him the truth. Nothing. One person. Fifteen seconds. A
items.prompt: A FILM PRODUCER BLOCKED ME MID-CONVERSATION OVER THIS SEEDANCE 2.0 CLIP I posted it privately in a group chat. He DM’d one question: “How much did this cost?” I told him the truth. Nothing. One person. Fifteen seconds. A stone dragon the size of a skyscraper breaking through the clouds. Two figures on a cliff watching it rise. Volumetric fog wrapping around carved scales. Light cutting through the clouds behind its head. The opening shot of a fantasy film that doesn’t exist. No studio greenlit it. No concept artist spent six months on the creature. No VFX house rendered it on a server farm for eight weeks. He said a single shot like this would take a team of forty and a $2 million minimum in VFX. For fifteen seconds. I showed him the prompt window. He said “that’s not possible,” then watched it three more times without a word. Last thing before he blocked me: “If this gets out, half my vendor list is dead.” Here’s the part that actually matters A shot like this doesn’t come from a lucky prompt. It comes from deciding the hard things before you generate - scale, atmosphere, and where the eye goes. 1. Scale is a framing choice, not a size slider. The dragon reads as skyscraper-sized because two tiny human figures are standing in frame to measure it against. Remove them and it’s just a big dragon; keep them and it’s an event 2. Atmosphere hides the seams and sells the scale. Volumetric fog wrapping the scales, clouds breaking around the head -the haze is doing half the work, giving the creature depth and letting the imagination fill in what the frame doesn’t show 3. Backlight is what makes it cinematic. Light cutting through the clouds behind the head turns a creature render into a reveal. The silhouette does more than the detail 4. A held moment beats a busy one. Two figures watching, a slow rise, no cut. Stillness is what makes something feel enormous -motion would shrink it Why this matters • The cost collapse is the whole story -a $2 million quote against one person and a subscription, for the same fifteen seconds • The producer’s reaction is the real signal: when someone with a vendor list watches it four times and goes quiet, the gap between “AI clip” and “studio shot” just got uncomfortably small • The barrier that dropped for one person dropped for everyone - which means the edge isn’t access to the tool, it’s knowing what to decide before you hit generate Worth being straight about • One shot is not a film - a stunning fifteen seconds is the easy part, and holding that quality across a whole sequence is where the real work still is • “$2 million, a team of forty” is the pitch, not an invoice -the honest comparison is capability, not an exact figure • A clip this close to real is exactly why the legal and vendor anxiety is showing up -worth taking seriously if you plan to publish His question was “how much did this cost.” The better one was “what did you decide before you hit generate.”

items.prompt: This might be the best synthetic performance I have got from a video model. We can generate 30-second shots and create near seamless extensions (with a bit of post blending) for far longer sequences, powered by @seedance 2.5. I set out to test this out by making the scene below all-in-one shot. I wrote the script, built the character references in Seedream and then broke the script down to two 30 second prompts. The prompts were really detailed with pauses, gestures and emotional shifts and the model delivered on all of them. I was really impressed with the performance and voices which were generated in the model. Previously, AI film scenes had to be composed of short cuts, now we have options on pacing, and nuance... we can let our scenes breathe. All this done with only around 3 rolls per take, we have left the slot machine age of AI video Gen behind and are now in the age of control. Next for me will be testing real actors performance as a reference to drive the generation. Seedance 2.5 API is about to launch on @BytePlusGlobal , and @lumina_ai_aiart will also roll out Seedance 2.5 soon.

We can generate 30-second shots and create near seamless extensions (with a bit of post blending) for far longer sequences, powered by @seedance 2.5. I set out to test this out by making the scene below all-in-one shot. I wrote the script, built the character references in Seedream and then broke the script down to two 30 second prompts. The prompts were really detailed with pauses, gestures and emotional shifts and the model delivered on all of them. I was really impressed with the performance and voices which were generated in the model. Previously, AI film scenes had to be composed of short cuts, now we have options on pacing, and nuance... we can let our scenes breathe. All this done with only around 3 rolls per take, we have left the slot machine age of AI video Gen behind and are now in the age of control. Next for me will be testing real actors performance as a reference to drive the generation. Seedance 2.5 API is about to launch on @BytePlusGlobal , and @lumina_ai_aiart will also roll out Seedance 2.5 soon.

Music-video route: dance/performance, rooftop golden-hour editorial. Track: industrial hip-hop, 95 BPM half-time, distorted 808s, luxury-noir. Director thesis: a skyline coronation — the lead and her four dancers own an empty rooftop at last light, silhouettes against the city. Visual world: flat concrete rooftop of a brutalist tower at golden hour, low sun raking long shadows across the roof, city skyline hazy in the background, wind moving fabric. Background dancers: 4 dancers in tonal rust and camel utilitarian looks, sculptural streetwear. Palette: golden amber, rust, concrete, bone white top cutting through, deep indigo. Natural light only, no neon, no particles. Cut map synced to @Audio1 : 0.0–2.0s THE BREATH — static ultra-wide from across the rooftop: five figures spread far apart in a pentagon, all facing the sun, long shadows pointing at camera. Wind and stillness. 2.0s THE DROP — 808 kick: all five pivot to camera in unison on the hit; hard cut to low-angle medium of the lead, sun flaring behind her braids. 2.0–4.0s she struts along the roof edge parapet line (safe, well inside the roof), the four dancers converging on her diagonally from the corners in lockstep, shadows sweeping like clock hands; camera dollying backward. 4.0s snare — whip-pan: full freeze in a tight cluster, she hits a profile vogue arm frame, dancers frozen in four different angular silhouettes against the skyline. 4.0–8.0s golden-hour choreography in medium-wide: her sharp head isolations and New Way vogue arm lines land on the snares; the four dancers frame her in rotating formations — box, diagonal, split pairs — changing formation exactly on each snare hit; torso rolls ripple through the group on the 808 slides. Camera orbits with the sun cross-lighting faces. 8.0s hi-hat triple roll — 3 rapid macro inserts: her earring flaring in backlight, four hands hitting the same vogue frame stacked in depth, boots pivoting on rooftop gravel. 8.5–12.0s escalation: accelerating orbital around the cluster as the dancers whip around her in a fast carousel, her solo arm work speeding up at the axis, long shadows strobing across the lens; speed-ramp slow-motion stretch — hair and fabric floating in wind — then snap back on the kick. 12.0s bass slide — the whole group drops level together into deep sliding lunges across the concrete, camera dutch and low, the sun skimming the roof surface. 13.5–15.0s FINAL BUTTON — hard cut to the opening ultra-wide: pentagon reformed but now all facing camera, the lead center in a frozen vogue pose one arm high, four dancers kneeling on one knee, five long shadows converging at the lens; micro push-in, hold. Loopable. Performance rules: lead stoic, owns the horizon; dancers precise, faces neutral. Continuity: same five people, same wardrobe, same rooftop and light. Audio intent: every cut and formation change on a hit of @Audio1 ; faint foley only (wind, gravel, fabric). Quality bar: expensive editorial music video, natural cinematic grade, no AI gloss, no glow, no lens-flare abuse.

items.prompt: Seedance 2.0 on Higgsfield AI Full open-sourced prompts & assets below: I've always been curious about how cinematic AI videos are actually made. Seeing every prompt, reference image, and generation setting made this one especially interesting. Prompt: @Image1 is the performer — preserve her exact identity: cornrow braids into long dark curls, silver chain-drop earring, gold pendant necklace, washed-green denim corset top, glossy lips. @Audio1 is the finished master track — the only audio; no invented music, no new vocals. SHE RAPS THE VOCAL ON CAMERA — PRECISE LIPSYNC IS THE TOP PRIORITY. Mouth articulates every syllable of @Audio1 exactly on time; face visible and sharp through every vocal line, no cutaways mid-word. LIPSYNC MAP: 0.0–0.5 instrumental. 0.5–2.8 "I'm standing on the edge / Say it with your chest / Or keep it on the deck" + "Hey!" 3.2–6.7 "I walk in, whole room gets tense / I don't need luck, I'm the consequence / If you really want to test my intent / Come correct, come correct or get bent" + "Woo!" 7.5–13.7 same hook verbatim second time, escalated. 14.5–15.0 instrumental hold. Music-video route: dance/performance, NYC caged basketball court. Director thesis: queen of the cage — she raps at the center of a chain-link basketball court while her girls run formations around her. Black girlie hustle vibe. Visual world: outdoor NYC basketball court wrapped in tall chain-link fence, faded court paint, brick housing blocks and fire escapes behind, late golden-hour sun throwing fence-diamond shadows across the asphalt. 4 background dancers: Black girls styled sharp — matching cropped white tanks, baggy cargo denim in different washes, bamboo hoops, colorful silk scarves tied on heads, clean Timberlands and Air Force 1s. items.prompt: THE AGENT THAT BUILT A FULL ANIMATED AD FROM ONE INSTRUCTION IN SEEDANCE 2.0 × GPT IMAGE 2.0 One prompt. One AI agent. A full 15-second chase-to-punchline commercial, from character sheets to final cut, with no manual shot-by-shot work. No re-prompting between shots. No building character references one by one. No stitching the sequence together by hand. Most people still treat AI video like a one-shot-at-a-time job — generate a frame, check it, generate the next, repeat until it's done. The real shift happens when you hand the whole pipeline to an agent that turns one instruction into tracked tasks and runs them at the same time. 1. Give the agent the full brief once — the characters you want, the tool stack, how many shots, the format and resolution 2. The agent builds a character sheet for each character in GPT Image 2.0 first — full body views, poses, close-ups, locked before any video gets made 3. The agent plans the shots itself — chase, standoff, reveal, sharing moment, each with its own timing 4. Every shot becomes its own task, generated on its own in Seedance 2.0 5. The agent checks in as each task finishes — accepting what's ready, flagging what's done, running the rest in parallel instead of waiting one by one 6. The last step stitches every finished shot into one sequence, product shot included, ready to post Why this works - Treating each shot as its own task means one bad generation doesn't hold up the rest - Locking the character sheets first is what keeps the officer, the thief, and the product looking the same across five different shots - Running shots in parallel cuts the total time way down - The agent handles the planning and checking, so your job becomes approving, not generating Use cases: ⁃ Branded or product-placement animated shorts ⁃ Multi-character sequences with dialogue and a clear story beat ⁃ Small teams wanting agency-level output without an agency ⁃ Testing a full commercial idea before spending a real budget on it One shot needed a redo because the officer's expression looked off in the standoff. Still one instruction in, one finished ad out — the agent did the part that used to take a whole team.

items.title: ChatGPT + Seedance 2.0 Workflow Step 1: Create a new ChatGPT project and upload everything you w
items.description: ChatGPT + Seedance 2.0 Workflow Step 1: Create a new ChatGPT project and upload everything you want the model to remember throughout the production, including character sheets, location references, style guides, product
items.prompt: ChatGPT + Seedance 2.0 Workflow Step 1: Create a new ChatGPT project and upload everything you want the model to remember throughout the production, including character sheets, location references, style guides, product references, story notes, and continuity rules. Step 2: Define the objective. Describe the story, commercial, trailer, or scene you want to create and explain the visual style, pacing, and overall creative direction. Step 3: Ask ChatGPT to break the story into multiple 5 to 10 second batches. Each batch should have a clearly defined start frame and end frame. The end frame of one batch must become the exact start frame of the next to maintain perfect continuity. Step 4: Ask ChatGPT to generate a detailed storyboard for every batch. Keep the same characters, costumes, props, lighting, scale, camera direction, and environment consistent across all frames. Step 5: Review the storyboard. Regenerate individual batches until every transition, action, and composition feels natural and continuous. Step 6: Once the storyboard is approved, ask ChatGPT to convert each batch into a professional Seedance 2.0 video prompt. Each prompt should include cinematography, camera movement, character performance, continuity rules, environment details, and animation instructions. Step 7: Generate every batch in Seedance 2.0. Render them in parallel for speed or one by one if you want to review each scene before continuing. Step 8: If any shot breaks continuity, regenerate only that specific batch while keeping the same start frame, end frame, characters, and visual style. Step 9: Stitch all generated clips together in chronological order. Since every batch shares matching transition frames, the complete video should play as one seamless, continuous sequence. Step 10: Perform the final edit by adding sound effects, music, dialogue, color grading, and any finishing touches before exporting the completed video.

items.prompt: The biggest shift in AI video isn’t just better visuals—it’s giving creators more control over what they can bring to life.🔥 It’s the amount of creative control that’s becoming available to creators. Better character consistency, smoother motion, stronger scene details, more natural expressions, and more cinematic camera movement can completely change the way we approach visual storytelling. Seedance 2.5 on @morphic is a great example of where this space is heading. The goal is no longer just to generate a cool-looking clip from a prompt. It’s about having enough control to actually bring a specific creative idea to life. Instead of spending most of the time regenerating clips and fixing inconsistencies, creators can spend more time experimenting with different concepts, characters, camera angles, environments, and stories. That opens up a lot of possibilities for filmmakers, marketers, content creators, and even people who have never worked with traditional video production before. AI video still has a long way to go, but the progress is becoming harder to ignore. The gap between imagining a scene and actually seeing it on screen keeps getting smaller. Now I’m really curious to see what creators do with Seedance 2.5 on @morphic. 🎬

items.prompt: Zero VFX experience. Just Claude, Seedance 2.0, and a phone clip. The result looks like a $10M scene In this tutorial you'll learn how to create cinematic AI VFX from your own real footage — no green screen, no masking, no compositing, no render times. Claude doesn't touch the video — it reads your clip frame by frame and writes the prompt, locking your face, camera move, light, and gestures, then naming the one thing to change and when. That prompt goes into Seedance 2.0, which only touches what was named. That's the trick. You're not describing an effect and hoping the AI gets it. Claude studies the footage first and hands Seedance a locked, precise instruction — which is why a hand can morph mid-sentence with zero visible cut, or neon reflections land on the dashboard automatically, with nothing graded by hand. One clip in, one sentence to Claude, one prompt into Seedance 2.0 — and out comes a shot that would normally cost a studio a month. ▪ 00:00 Intro ▪ 01:28 The 3 levels of AI VFX ▪ 01:59 Level 1 — Swapping the world (walking) ▪ 04:32 Level 2 — Changing an element ▪ 07:26 Level 3 — The handheld showcase ▪ 10:15 Outro YouTube: "Higgsfield AI - I Added Insane AI VFX to Real Footage in 4K(Seedance 2.0)" Thank you for sharing this free tutorial with us. items.prompt: Seedance 2.0 on Vidfield AI Prompt: "Create a 15-second realistic cinematic slice-of-life video in 16:9, 24fps. Visual-only video, no dialogue, no voice, no music, no sound effects, no subtitles, no text on screen. Warm golden-hour sunlight, soft handheld camera, muted film color grade, slight grain, natural shadows, peaceful nostalgic neighborhood mood. Fully realistic live-action style, not game-like, not animated. Main character: a young Korean woman in her early 20s with messy dark brown hair tied in a loose ponytail, soft natural face, calm gentle expression, dark gray cropped sleeveless tank top, loose light-wash blue jeans, black necklace, casual sneakers. Keep her look consistent in every shot. Location: a long narrow real-life residential alley between tall tan stone and concrete walls. Sandy dusty ground, warm sunlight glowing on one side, soft tree shadows across the path, palm trees and green leaves visible above the walls, a blue painted wall far ahead, one bicycle leaning near the end of the alley, quiet empty neighborhood feeling. 0:00–0:02: Rear tracking shot. The Korean woman walks slowly through the long narrow alley from behind. Golden sunlight stretches across the tan walls. Camera follows with natural handheld motion. 0:02–0:04: Wide alley shot. A small gray-brown tabby cat appears from a low gap near the left side wall and steps into the alley. The woman notices it, slows down, and turns slightly toward it. 0:04–0:06: Medium side shot. The cat walks near her feet and looks up. She smiles softly, bends down slowly, and extends one hand in a gentle careful way. 0:06–0:08: Low close-up. The cat sniffs her fingers, then rubs its head against her hand. She gently pets the cat’s head and back. Show realistic fur texture, tiny whisker movement, and natural cat behavior. 0:08–0:10: Emotional close-up. The woman smiles warmly while petting the cat. Sunlight flickers through tree leaves across her face, shoulders, and hair. Keep the moment soft, calm, and human. 0:10–0:12: Medium-wide shot. The cat walks ahead a few steps, then looks back at her. She stands slowly and follows it with a curious peaceful smile. 0:12–0:14: Front tracking shot. She walks toward camera with the cat beside her near the wall. She looks down at the cat and smiles. The long alley, tan walls, blue wall far behind, trees, and bicycle remain visible. 0:14–0:15: Final close shot. The cat brushes against her leg. She looks toward the camera with a soft peaceful smile, then looks down at the cat again. Hold the warm golden alley atmosphere for a gentle cinematic ending."

items.prompt: YOU HAVE BEEN TRAINED TO TRUST A PHOTO YOUR OWN EYES CAN NO LONGER VERIFY That queso smash on the sign outside? It was never plated, never cooked, never real. It was generated by a prompt, approved by a manager who thought nobody would notice. > menu boards, delivery apps, and social platforms are increasingly running AI-generated food photography instead of real shots - Forkable, a US catering platform, quietly swapped real restaurant photos for AI images across its entire site without telling the restaurants themselves > McDonald's Netherlands pulled a fully AI-generated Christmas ad within days of backlash, proof that even a billion-dollar brand can't out-market the moment customers spot the uncanny gloss of a synthetic image > under the FTC's "reasonable consumer standard," AI food imagery can legally count as false advertising the moment it materially changes what someone expected to receive - a disclaimer buried in fine print doesn't erase that > the deception now runs both directions: some customers use AI-edited photos of "raw" or "moldy" food to fraud their way into refunds, forcing DoorDash and other platforms to build detection systems just to catch fabricated evidence > researchers call this a live regulatory blind spot - almost no jurisdiction has updated food fraud law to cover AI-generated imagery, meaning there is currently very little legal deterrent for either the restaurant or the customer How to actually spot it before you order: > look for unnaturally perfect symmetry - real melted cheese pulls unevenly, AI cheese pulls in a suspiciously smooth arc > check the shadows - AI food photos often have lighting that doesn't match the direction of any visible light source > zoom in on garnish and texture - AI still struggles with fine details like sesame seed placement, herb sprigs, or steam > search the exact dish name plus the restaurant on Reddit or Instagram - real customer photos will contradict the marketing fast You were taught to trust your eyes at the counter. Now the eyes need training too.

Camera: a vertical top-down POV chase-cam, diving straight down in perfect sync with his fall, creating a vertigo-inducing straight-down perspective the entire beat. items.prompt: Dance rehearsal mini vlog created using Seedance 2.0 Prompt: Format: 16:9 Concept: "Behind the Choreography" Create a hyper-realistic self-recorded vlog filmed entirely on a modern flagship smartphone using the front-facing camera. The entire video is captured by the idol herself in one continuous take, creating an authentic behind-the-scenes experience. The footage should feel completely unscripted, with natural handheld movement, subtle smartphone stabilization, realistic autofocus breathing, automatic HDR exposure adjustments, occasional imperfect framing, and genuine ambient sound. No cinematic shots, jump cuts, transitions, slow motion, or stylized editing. Visual Style Modern smartphone video with crisp 4K detail, realistic HDR, balanced indoor lighting, true-to-life colours, natural skin texture, and clean image processing. No filters, no beauty mode, no film grain, and no artificial cinematic effects. It should look exactly like a real selfie vlog filmed on a flagship phone. Character YURI, a Korean female idol in her twenties with long black hair tied into a neat high ponytail, minimal rehearsal makeup, naturally glowing skin, and an energetic, cheerful personality. She wears realistic dance practice clothing: an oversized charcoal zip-up hoodie over a fitted black athletic top, loose grey sweatpants, white sneakers, and a smartwatch. During rehearsal, she removes the hoodie and ties it around her waist, matching a real dance studio environment. Location A professional K-pop dance practice studio with mirrored walls, polished wooden floors, ceiling speakers, bright rehearsal lighting, backpacks, water bottles, towels, portable fans, and dancers warming up naturally in the background. The recording starts just outside the practice room. YURI smiles at the phone. "Come with me... today you get to see what rehearsal actually looks like." She opens the studio door and walks inside, greeting the dancers with a quick wave before placing her backpack beside the mirror. She stretches while chatting casually to the camera. "Everyone sees the performance... but not this part." The music starts. She removes her hoodie, ties it around her waist, and joins the rehearsal. items.prompt: Seedance 2.0 on Social sight Ai Try it with prompt : FORMAT 15 seconds | 16:9 | live-action military documentary footage Fictional aircraft-carrier emergency at sea. Hyper-realistic raw footage. Fast multi-shot storytelling across handheld, telephoto and deck cameras. STORY A carrier-based fighter returns over rough open water with an apparent mechanical problem. The flight deck enters emergency recovery mode. Crew clear the landing area as the fighter approaches and lands safely. 00–03s — EMERGENCY Wide handheld footage on an active carrier deck under heavy overcast skies. Strong sea wind, grey ocean, wet worn deck. Crew receive an alert and urgently clear the landing area. One crew member signals others away as the camera quickly turns toward the ocean. 03–06s — FINAL APPROACH Hard cut to long telephoto footage. A fictional fighter approaches low over the ocean, landing gear down. Aircraft makes subtle roll and yaw corrections against turbulent air. Heat distortion behind engines. Camera operator struggles slightly to maintain framing. 06–09s — DECK SCRAMBLE Shoulder-mounted footage among crew. Personnel rapidly move equipment and take safe positions. One crew member crosses foreground, briefly blocking the lens. Camera pans toward the approaching fighter. Controlled professional urgency, no theatrical panic. 09–12s — TOUCHDOWN Low deck camera from a safe side position. Fighter touches down firmly. Landing gear compresses, tyres produce a small realistic puff, aircraft rapidly decelerates. Camera makes a fast imperfect pan following it. No explosion or exaggerated sparks. 12–15s — SAFE STOP Three-quarter handheld footage. Aircraft reaches a controlled stop, engine still running and heat haze visible. Crew cautiously approach, signal toward the cockpit and inspect the aircraft. Final frame holds briefly on the fighter surrounded by responding crew with rough ocean behind. CAMERA Real military documentation/news footage. Mix handheld deck camera, shoulder-mounted footage, long telephoto tracking and fixed low deck camera. Hard cuts. Reactive pans. Foreground obstruction. Autofocus corrections. Telephoto compression. Wind-induced micro-shake. Natural motion blur. Camera operators react to events rather than anticipating them. ENVIRONMENT Working aircraft carrier in rough open ocean. Wet non-slip deck, painted markings, deck equipment, parked fictional aircraft, heavy clouds and strong maritime wind. PHYSICS Aircraft has convincing mass, momentum and aerodynamic behaviour. Approach remains aligned with the carrier. Landing gear compresses naturally. Deceleration has believable inertia. Crew clothing and straps react continuously to wind. Jet engines produce realistic heat distortion. AUDIO Powerful wind, ocean ambience, carrier machinery, shouted instructions, approaching jet roar, tyre contact, aircraft deceleration and crew communication. Sound perspective changes naturally between shots. No cinematic soundtrack. VISUAL CHARACTER Raw live-action military footage. Photorealistic aircraft, crew and ocean. Natural overcast exposure. Weathered equipment. Atmospheric haze. Sensor noise and minor camera imperfections. No CGI appearance. No video-game aesthetic. No Hollywood treatment. No slow motion. No oversized explosions. No impossible camera movement. CONTINUITY Same fictional fighter, carrier, weather, deck and crew throughout. Aircraft direction and position remain geographically consistent. Every shot advances the same emergency landing chronologically.

items.description: THE KITSUNE BLADE SEQUENCE — SEEDANCE 2.0 + GPT IMAGE 2 STORYBOARD One fox warrior. A minimal white studio backdrop. Every slash reads clean because nothing in the frame is fighting for attention. Most creators build a c
items.prompt: THE KITSUNE BLADE SEQUENCE — SEEDANCE 2.0 + GPT IMAGE 2 STORYBOARD One fox warrior. A minimal white studio backdrop. Every slash reads clean because nothing in the frame is fighting for attention. Most creators build a character like this and then generate the fight scene straight from a single hero image hoping Seedance guesses the choreography. It doesn't - you get a great character standing in a great pose cut after cut, never actually fighting. Here's the workflow 1. Build the character concept and lock it in GPT Image 2 first- golden fox ears, long amber hair, flowing gold-and-black robe, calm amber eyes hiding controlled aggression, proportions and fabric behavior fixed before motion enters the picture 2. Build a separate storyboard per scene instead of one giant grid -stillness gets its own board, the charge gets its own, the strike and the aftermath each get their own. More room per panel for camera notes, and one scene can be revised without touching the rest 3. Strip the environment down to a plain white/grey studio backdrop, and let the sword carry the energy instead - a single glowing gold trail following the blade does more for "power" than any explosion behind her would 4. Merge the boards into one sheet only at the end, purely for review and to fit the whole sequence into a single reference video - actual generation still pulls from each scene's board individually 5. Animate each scene from its own storyboard in Seedance 2.0 as a staging and camera-movement reference only, with likeness anchored to the GPT Image 2 sheet throughout Why this works - Splitting boards by scene means every camera setup gets enough space to actually be planned, not crammed into a tiny panel - The glowing blade trail becomes the character's signature -consistent across every cut because it's designed once, not improvised per shot - Each scene can be regenerated or refined on its own without disturbing the sequence around it - The calm extreme close-up after the burst is what sells "predator at rest" - stillness after violence hits harder than more violence would Made with GPT Image 2 (storyboard) + Seedance 2.0 (animation). Full reference sheet + prompt in the comments below↓

items.prompt: WHY MOST AI CHARACTERS BREAK BY SCENE 3 — SEEDANCE 2.0 + CHATGPT IMAGE 2 A creator renders the same character across three Seedance 2.0 scenes. Expects it to look like one story. Instead the jacket changes. The blade changes color. The face drifts. By scene three, it’s not the same person anymore. The render didn’t break it. The prep did. Most multi-location clips fall apart because the character changes shape between scenes. Face close enough. Outfit close enough. Nothing actually matches once the clips sit side by side. The people getting clean results aren’t prompting harder per scene. They lock the character once in ChatGPT Image 2. Then build a separate location atlas for every environment — before a single clip gets generated. Character design sheet comes first. Full turnaround, expressions, silhouette study, detail crops. Built once. Reused across every scene. Never regenerated per location. Each location gets its own atlas: Wide establishing shot Camera path diagram Lighting study Material swatches Environment-specific details (dust behavior, ember flow) Camera path gets planned before generation, not guessed inside the Seedance prompt. An orbit diagram or push-in path drawn in advance keeps motion intentional instead of improvised. Lighting stays location-specific, character stays consistent. A red blade reads differently in desert daylight, golden-hour field, and volcanic interior. The character’s silhouette and proportions never shift. Where this breaks: Skipping the design sheet and regenerating the character fresh per location. Small drifts stack fast — hair length, jacket detail, blade color — and by scene three it’s obviously not the same person. The other failure: one long Seedance prompt for the whole scene instead of anchoring each location with its own reference frame first. Seedance only extends what the frame gives it. No locked character, no planned path — motion has nothing stable to build on. The gap between a clean multi-location clip and a broken one isn’t the render. It’s everything decided before the render starts. Full guide — zero to finished cinematic video — below 🔖

items.prompt: THE SHOT THAT MAKES A LOCKED CHARACTER FEEL LIKE A REAL PERSON The character sheet was already perfect. The video is what proves it. Most creators lock a character sheet in GPT Image 2 and think the job is done. The real test only happens once that character has to move hold a blade and turn toward camera without a single detail slipping. Here's the workflow 1. Build the character concept -a cyber-oni android warrior, pale porcelain skin silver-white hair, twin ivory horns one robotic arm with crimson claw-tips katana in black-and-red wrap 2. Lock the full reference sheet in GPT Image 2 - front/side/back turnaround, detail callouts on face, neck mechanism, blade, and claws, plus a color palette 3. Draft a shot-by-shot sequence - silhouette open → slow orbit reveal → blade motion → extreme close-up on the eyes → wide hero stand on reflective ground 4. Repeat the identity-lock line in every single shot prompt- face, horns, coat emblem, and robotic arm called out by name, not left to the reference image alone 5. Keep the environment palette consistent - deep red sky, black smoke, reflective black ground - so lighting never resets between cuts 6. Let the close-up shots do the identity-proofing -eyes and face detail are where drift shows first so give them dedicated frames 7. Animate the full sequence in Seedance 2.0 straight from the locked sheet + shot list Why this works: • The robotic arm and horn shape stay identical from the wide shot to the extreme close-up • Red accent lighting carries through every cut instead of shifting tone • The blade's wrap pattern and tsuba stay recognizable even in fast motion • Eyes hold the same iris detail in close-up as they did in the reference sheet • Way fewer regenerations per shot Use cases: ⁃ Character showcase reels ⁃ Game trailer teasers ⁃ Original IP / OC promotional content ⁃ Dark fantasy and cyberpunk short films ⁃ Style-driven AI video demos The character sheet answers who she is. This is what proves she's real.

Black hair loosely tied back with soft bangs and a few loose strands moving in the breeze. Minimal makeup. Faded cream sleeveless top. Loose light-blue jeans. Worn canvas sneakers. Consistent identity throughout. Location Authentic rural Chinese village on a warm summer afternoon. Whitewashed walls. Grey tiled roofs. Vegetable garden. Stone pathways. Bamboo baskets. Clay pots. Citrus trees. Laundry hanging outside. Wooden courtyard gate. Quiet countryside atmosphere. No commercial elements. Visual Style Ultra-realistic memory-like documentary footage. Feels like a family member casually recording moments during a visit. Sharp facial detail. Natural skin texture. Realistic lighting. Authentic environmental motion. High-quality image. No cinematic color grading. No exaggerated vintage effects. No obvious AI look. The footage should feel genuinely recorded rather than generated. Camera Treatment Consumer digital camera from approximately 2008–2012. Handheld but mostly stable. Natural human movement while filming. Occasional framing imperfections. Minor focus breathing. Subtle exposure adaptation when moving between sunlight and shade. No excessive shake. No heavy blur. No strong digital noise. No aggressive autofocus hunting. The camera supports the memory rather than drawing attention to itself. 00:00–00:02 The camera follows her entering through a wooden courtyard gate. She notices her grandmother watering vegetables and immediately smiles. The camera lingers naturally as she walks toward her. 00:02–00:04 Grandmother is watering a small vegetable patch. The young woman gently takes the watering can and helps. Both laugh naturally. A light breeze moves nearby plants. 00:04–00:06 Grandmother points toward something growing among the vegetables. The young woman crouches beside her to look. Sunlight filters through leaves overhead. Small authentic gestures and eye contact. 00:06–00:08 In the courtyard. Grandmother hands her a fresh orange segment. She tastes it and smiles. The camera quietly observes the moment without interruption. 00:08–00:10 They fold laundry together beside a clothesline. Fabric moves gently in the summer breeze. Conversation continues naturally. No posing. 00:10–00:12 Sitting together on small stools beneath shade. Grandmother says something amusing. The young woman laughs and leans slightly toward her. The moment feels completely unplanned. 00:12–00:15 Leaving through the courtyard gate carrying a small bag of fruit. Halfway down the path she turns around. Her grandmother is still standing there watching. They exchange one final wave. The camera remains still for a moment after she turns away. Recording ends naturally. Audio Birds. Distant village ambience. Wind through trees. Laundry fluttering. Footsteps on stone. Quiet conversation. Occasional chicken sounds. No music. No narration. No sound design. Generation Goal A real family memory unexpectedly preserved on a camera. Warm. Ordinary. Deeply human. The viewer should feel like they are watching somebody's genuine childhood memory.

items.prompt: Seedance 2.0 on Vidfield AI Prompt: Create a 15-second realistic cinematic slice-of-life video in 16:9, 24fps. Visual-only video, no dialogue, no voice, no music, no sound effects, no subtitles, no text on screen. Warm golden-hour sunlight, soft handheld camera, muted film color grade, slight grain, natural shadows, peaceful nostalgic mood. Fully realistic live-action style, not game-like, not animated. Main character: a young Japanese woman in her early 20s with soft natural features, dark hair tied in a loose low bun with a small traditional hairpin. She wears elegant traditional Japanese attire: a simple cream-and-muted-blue yukata/kimono-style outfit with a subtle floral pattern, tied with a soft obi belt, light tabi-style sandals. Keep her calm, gentle, warm expression consistent in every shot. Location: a long narrow real-life residential alley with a Japanese touch. Tall tan stone and concrete walls, sandy dusty ground, warm sunlight glowing on one side, soft tree shadows across the path, palm trees and green leaves above the walls, small Japanese details like a wooden gate, paper lantern near a doorway, simple noren curtain, potted bonsai-style plants, and a blue painted wall far ahead. One bicycle leans near the end of the alley. Quiet empty neighborhood feeling. 0:00–0:02: Rear tracking shot. The Japanese woman walks slowly through the narrow alley from behind. Her yukata fabric moves gently as she walks. Golden sunlight stretches across the tan walls. Camera follows with natural handheld motion. 0:02–0:04: Wide alley shot. A small gray-brown tabby cat appears from a low gap near the left side wall and steps into the alley. The woman notices it, slows down, and turns slightly toward it. 0:04–0:06: Medium side shot. The cat walks near her feet and looks up. She smiles softly, bends down slowly, and extends one hand in a gentle careful way. 0:06–0:08: Low close-up. The cat sniffs her fingers, then rubs its head against her hand. She gently pets the cat’s head and back. Show realistic fur texture, tiny whisker movement, and natural cat behavior. 0:08–0:10: Emotional close-up. The woman smiles warmly while petting the cat. Sunlight flickers through tree leaves across her face, hairpin, shoulders, and kimono fabric. 0:10–0:12: Medium-wide shot. The cat walks ahead a few steps, then looks back at her. She stands slowly and follows it with a peaceful curious smile. The Japanese alley details remain subtle and realistic. 0:12–0:14: Front tracking shot. She walks toward camera with the cat beside her near the wall. She looks down at the cat and smiles. The long alley, tan walls, Japanese details, blue wall, bicycle, and trees remain visible in the background. 0:14–0:15: Final close shot. The cat brushes against her leg. She looks toward the camera with a soft peaceful smile, then looks down at the cat again. Hold the warm golden Japanese alley atmosphere for a gentle cinematic ending.

items.prompt: Looks like a blockbuster police chase, but every frame was generated with AI. This is the future of AI filmmaking. Seedance 2.0 4K Prompt: Maintain a consistent environment, vehicles, police uniforms, and motorcycle throughout the video. The setting is a modern city highway bridge during daylight. The chase is fast, cinematic, and high tension. Maintain seamless continuity between all scenes with smooth camera transitions. Style: Cinematic action thriller, realistic vehicle physics, dynamic camera movement, premium movie quality, dramatic lighting, high-speed motion, realistic traffic, aerial cinematography, shallow depth of field, 8K cinematic rendering. Audio: Intense cinematic chase score, continuous police sirens, motorcycle engine revving, tire noise, wind, passing traffic. No dialogue. Scene 1 (0–2s) A wide aerial view looks down at a long highway bridge filled with moving traffic. A convoy of police cars with flashing red and blue lights races across the bridge with sirens blaring as they pursue a single motorcycle weaving through traffic. Camera: High-altitude drone shot slowly descending toward the chase. Scene 2 (2–4s) The camera dives closer to the bridge before cutting to a helmet-mounted perspective from the motorcyclist. The rider rapidly approaches slower traffic while police vehicles remain visible in the mirrors with flashing lights. Camera: First-person helmet camera with realistic speed and motion. Scene 3 (4–6.5s) The view transitions to a cinematic tracking shot beside the motorcycle. The rider expertly leans through traffic, squeezing between cars and overtaking vehicles at high speed while maintaining control. Camera: Smooth side tracking shot followed by a low front angle. Scene 4 (6.5–9s) The police convoy attempts to follow but is slowed by heavy traffic. Patrol cars brake, change lanes, and struggle to keep up because they cannot fit through the narrow gaps that the motorcycle easily passes. Camera: Alternating shots from behind the police cars, overhead drone views, and low roadside tracking shots. Scene 5 (9–12s) The motorcycle accelerates even faster, weaving through the final stretch of traffic. The distance between the rider and the police grows rapidly as the bridge opens ahead. Camera: Dynamic orbit around the motorcycle, then a tracking shot from in front as the rider speeds toward the end of the bridge. Scene 6 (12–15s) A wide cinematic aerial shot shows the motorcycle racing toward the distant horizon at the far end of the bridge while the police convoy falls farther behind. The flashing lights become smaller as the rider disappears into the distance, leaving the pursuit behind. Camera: Slow pullback aerial shot ending with the motorcycle fading toward the horizon. Visual Keywords Cinematic police pursuit, modern highway bridge, realistic traffic, high-speed motorcycle chase, police convoy, flashing emergency lights, realistic vehicle physics, dynamic action cinematography, aerial drone shots, helmet POV, smooth camera transitions, dramatic motion blur, premium action film quality, intense atmosphere, seamless storytelling, 8K cinematic realism.

items.prompt: the client is not buying a render they are buying the moment they can finally make a decision. that is why this kind of AI visual work is a real business. look at the workflow: a rough property photo goes in. then the same space gets tested as a renovated version, a cleaner layout, a different mood, a different buyer story. that used to be a slow back-and-forth with a studio. now one operator can turn the ugly first version into a client-ready direction before the meeting even happens. this is where AI fits in architecture. not the stamped drawing. not the permit set. not structural responsibility. the money is upstream: - concept visuals - renovation previews - moodboards - layout options - client decks - fast iterations before the expensive phase starts full-service architecture firms charge $15k-$80k. but the pre-design layer can be sold separately. show the client the version they cannot imagine yet. then hand the buildable work to licensed professionals. that is the wedge. not AI replaced architects. items.prompt: 📖YOU COULD BE USING SEEDANCE 2.0 WRONGLY AND HERE'S WHY Three models were tested: GPT, Gemini and Claude and the difference is greater than expected Three models. One task. Write a cinematic prompt for AI video. Here's what each one does differently: • ChatGPT 5.4 — The Strategist GPT-5.4 approaches a prompt like an analyst. It breaks everything down into structured blocks: subject → action → environment → lighting → mood → camera movement. The result is clean, logical, and technically precise. The downside? It can feel a little cold. There's control and predictability, but sometimes less creative fire. Best when you want exact, repeatable results. - Strength: structure, accuracy, fewer hallucinations Weakness: less emotional charge, reads more like a brief than a vision • Gemini 3.5 — The Director Gemini 3.5 thinks like someone standing on a film set. It factors in scene context, motion physics, and atmosphere — prompts come out with details like "ice shards catching the light as the blade cuts through" or "hair trailing in slow motion against a frozen horizon." The native multimodality makes it naturally think in visuals before the video even exists. The result feels alive and cinematic. - Strength: cinematic thinking, physical detail, atmosphere Weakness: prompts can run long and overly descriptive • Claude Opus 4.7 — The Storyteller Opus 4.7 writes a prompt the way a novelist would. It builds in emotion, inner state, and narrative — and that shows up in the output. Where GPT gives technical precision and Gemini gives cinematic imagery, Claude gives feeling. Prompts are often shorter but denser in meaning. Videos generated from them tend to carry a more human quality. - Strength: emotional depth, narrative, style Weakness: fewer hard technical specs for complex scenes Bottom line: Need precision → GPT 5.4 Need cinematic quality → Gemini 3.5 Need soul → Claude Opus 4.7 How do you write prompts? What do you use? 📥Tomorrow I will make another comparison, but for now I will not reveal the secret which 🔖Below is a guide to using Dreamina for beginners

items.prompt: Meta just launched its 1st image model after Mark Zuckerberg’s AI shake-up. Muse Image is Meta Superintelligence Labs' first image generator after Muse Spark. They said the model will power new editing features in Meta’s Instagram photo app and be added to its marketer tools for creating platform ads. Meta had relied on Midjourney and Black Forest Labs for generation inside Meta AI. Muse Image brings that layer in-house, so Meta controls quality, cost, and product timing. Consumers get free access through Meta AI, WhatsApp chats, and Instagram Stories. Power users need Meta One or another monthly plan when free limits run out. Users can start from prompts, add photos, annotate edits, or sketch changes directly. Meta says it can erase photobombers, create QR codes, and keep visual text readable. Advertisers get variants through Advantage+ creative, with edits, style swaps, and brand-matched versions. Meta says internal tests trail GPT Image 2 but beat Nano Banana 2 on editing. This is another move in Meta's effort in trying to convert AI infrastructure spending into revenue beyond social ads.

items.prompt: I love this tracking shot style. Tracking the creature into destined character. I am using Seedance 2.0 on @dreamina_ai with only 1 image and 1 prompt ⬇️ PROMPT: Single continuous uninterrupted cinematic shot, no cuts, one flowing 15-second take. Desaturated cool palette with warm amber accents, deep shadow falloff, fine 35mm grain. Photorealistic live-action film, NOT animated, NOT a video game, NOT CGI render. A tense body-horror transformation at an archaeological expedition dig site in a vast sun-scorched desert at harsh midday, heat shimmer, drifting sand and dust. The shot opens at extreme ground level on a SMALL black desert scorpion — only palm-sized, realistic natural scale — ALREADY sprinting at full speed across the sand from the very first frame, mid-run, never stationary, the camera tracking low and fast right beside it. It races across open ground, weaving past scattered expedition gear — brushes, trowels, open crates, ropes, dusty boots of crew members — a long fast ground-level chase. Still in the same unbroken shot, the small scorpion reaches a man crouched at the dig — the man [IMAGE REFERENCE], in a dusty khaki expedition field shirt with rolled sleeves, utility vest, cargo pants and glasses. He holds a small ancient artifact up in both hands close to his face, calm and completely unaware, carefully examining and inspecting its fine details, turning it slowly to study the carvings, fully absorbed and fascinated by the small relic. The scorpion suddenly leaps onto the back of his hand. ONLY at the moment it lands does he react — he flinches hard, startled. The camera stays locked on the scorpion, following it closely as it scurries fast up his forearm, over his shoulder, onto his neck, and jabs its stinger hard into his neck. Only now does the camera ease back slightly to a medium shot: he cries out, slaps the scorpion off and flings it away, stumbling to his feet, gripping his neck in pain and confusion. Glowing sickly yellow-green venom veins spread from the sting across his neck and face as he convulses, his body warping and hardening into a monstrous humanoid scorpion creature — glossy dark chitinous exoskeleton with segmented armored plates, serrated pincers forming from his hands, glowing venomous yellow-green eyes, a massive segmented scorpion tail with a dripping stinger arching over his back. The shot stays close for the finale — a raw handheld medium shot, the camera shaking and reactive like real documentary footage, staying tight on the creature as it screeches and rampages through the dig site, thrashing its pincers and tail, knocking over crates and equipment, while terrified crew members in matching khaki outfits sprint past the camera in panic, dust kicking up, the handheld camera jostling among the chaos, gritty and real. No aerial view, no wide shot — stay in the chaos at ground level until the end. No music. #DreaminaCPP

items.prompt: Korean Couple Morning Routine (Mid-2010s Smartphone Style) Seedance 2.0 on OpenArt AI Prompt: Main subject: Young Korean couple, both early-to-mid 20s, fresh-faced and naturally attractive. Woman: long dark hair in a loose low bun with strands falling out, wearing an oversized soft beige hoodie and black bike shorts, glowing skin. Man: short textured black hair, wearing a white sleeveless tank and grey sweatpants, gentle and playful vibe. Keep their looks, outfits, and loving chemistry perfectly consistent across shots. Location: Charming Seoul suburban residential area at golden sunrise. Winding alleyways between colorful low-rise apartments, rooftop gardens with flowers, small balconies with drying clothes, steam from breakfast drifting out windows, birds on power lines, warm sunlight painting everything in soft orange and pink hues. Visual Style: Bright, heartwarming lifestyle realism with a dreamy morning glow. Soft bokeh in backgrounds, gentle lens flares from rising sun, vibrant yet natural colors, cozy and aspirational feel that makes viewers smile and feel warm inside. Focus on tender couple connection, small joyful gestures, and the beauty of simple shared moments. Camera Style: Mid-2010s smartphone video aesthetic (like an old iPhone 6 or Galaxy S5 recording). Casual vertical or slightly tilted handheld footage from one of them holding the phone. Light digital stabilization with occasional jitters, smooth but imperfect panning, auto white-balance shifts, subtle lens flare from morning sun, minor compression artifacts, natural color grading with slightly boosted warmth, occasional finger in frame or thumb occlusion at edges. No professional moves, feels like personal couple vlog footage. 00:00–00:02 Close-up of them waking up together on a small bed by the window. She sleepily smiles and pulls him in for a morning kiss on the forehead. Golden sunrise light pours in. 00:02–00:04 In their tiny kitchen, he makes coffee while she hugs him from behind, resting her chin on his shoulder. They sway together laughing as the coffee brews. 00:04–00:06 Stepping out to their small balcony. They feed leftover rice to birds on the railing. items.prompt: MOST PEOPLE ARE PROMPTING SEEDANCE 2.0 LIKE IT’S A SEARCH BAR AND IT’S COSTING THEM One simple structural change fixes most of the inconsistency. You know the cycle: write a sentence, hit generate, hate it, rewrite the whole thing from scratch. Most of us have been stuck there. The creators getting consistent results ditched that approach months ago. They treat prompts more like a production brief — every piece handled separately instead of crammed into one wall of text. Break it down like this: • Character identity • Environment + visual style • Camera behavior • Action sequence + pacing • Transitions That’s honestly it. Why it works so well: • Your character actually stays consistent across shots • Camera moves feel intentional instead of drunk • You can tweak one thing without breaking everything else • It turns into a reusable template for the whole series Simple workflow: 1. Decide what the video actually needs to say 2. Nail the character description once, in detail 3. Define environment/style as its own block 4. Write action and camera separately 5. Combine them cleanly Example: Character — hooded dragon knight Environment — misty ash-covered ruins Action — crouching, reaching for the eggs Camera — slow handheld push-in Style — cinematic, desaturated, 24fps Once you have this, the next scene isn’t a full rewrite. You just change one field. We’re moving from “prompting” to “designing a system.” The future of AI video isn’t a better sentence — it’s a structure you reuse instead of rebuild every time. More on what sits next to this soon. Full breakdown in the thread above — steal it before everyone else catches on.

Slight hand shake, occasional focus hunting, imperfect framing, natural zoom adjustments, soft tape-like image quality, subtle grain, realistic auto-exposure shifts from morning window light. Natural skin tones, mild motion blur, authentic consumer camcorder aesthetic. STYLE: Cozy study-desk vlog with gentle ASMR elements. Relaxed pacing, minimal dialogue, candid moments. "This is my favorite time of day." → (1.5s, final shot) Reaches toward camera. "See you after class." Hand covers lens. AUDIO NOTES: Natural room ambience grinder, pouring water, page turns, pen clicks, keyboard taps should be clearly audible. Dialogue quiet and casual. items.prompt: Seedance 2.0 on @higgsfield PROMPT ⬇ Use my uploaded character sheet as the ONLY reference for the character. Preserve the exact facial features, hairstyle, body proportions, skin tone, and identity throughout the entire video. The character must remain perfectly consistent. Do NOT change the face, body, or hairstyle. Only the outfit and environment change. Create a premium 15-second cinematic travel-fashion commercial where the character journeys through seven iconic countries. Every transition is triggered by the character touching or adjusting her outfit. As the outfit transforms, the entire environment seamlessly changes into the next country. The camera follows the character in one continuous cinematic shot with smooth movement and no cuts. Sequence: ① France 🇫🇷 The character wears an elegant Parisian luxury outfit. She gently adjusts her blazer collar. As she pulls the collar into place, her outfit transforms into the next country's traditional fashion while the Eiffel Tower and the streets of Paris seamlessly become the next location. ② Japan 🇯🇵 She now wears a modern luxury kimono-inspired outfit. She gently holds one sleeve and spins gracefully. During the spin, both her outfit and the scenery transform into South Korea. Background: Gyeongbokgung Palace with Seoul skyline. ③ South Korea 🇰🇷 She wears a modern designer hanbok-inspired outfit. She lightly smooths the front of her jacket. As her hand moves downward, the outfit transforms while the palace becomes the streets of Italy. Background: Colosseum and Rome cityscape. ④ Italy 🇮🇹 She wears elegant Italian luxury fashion. She adjusts her sunglasses and smiles confidently. As she lowers her hand, both the outfit and scenery transform. Background: Colosseum and classic Roman architecture. ⑤ United Arab Emirates 🇦🇪 She now wears a luxurious modern abaya-inspired couture outfit. She gently lifts the flowing fabric. As it falls, the environment transforms. Background: Burj Khalifa and Downtown Dubai at sunset. ⑥ India 🇮🇳 She wears an elegant contemporary designer saree. She gracefully adjusts the pallu over her shoulder. During the motion, the outfit transforms once more. Background: Taj Mahal during golden hour. ⑦ United States 🇺🇸 (Final Hero Scene) She now wears premium New York luxury street fashion. She confidently walks toward the camera as Times Square and the New York skyline surround her. The camera slowly pushes in while she gives a confident smile, ending with a premium fashion-commercial hero shot. Every transition is physically motivated by touching, adjusting, pulling, or spinning the clothing. The outfit and environment transform simultaneously with seamless cinematic match cuts, realistic fabric simulation, and premium architectural morphing. Camera: One continuous tracking shot, smooth dolly movement, occasional orbit, 50mm and 85mm cinematic lenses, shallow depth of field. Lighting: Natural golden-hour lighting adapted to each country with realistic reflections, soft rim lighting, and cinematic atmosphere. Style: Luxury Louis Vuitton, Dior, Gucci, Chanel global fashion campaign mixed with National Geographic travel cinematography. Ultra-realistic, premium editorial quality, flawless fabric physics, authentic architecture, 8K HDR, award-winning commercial cinematography, smooth transitions, no glitches, no text, no watermark.

items.prompt: ONE SPIN AND SHE'S A DIFFERENT PERSON. Seedance 2.0 Prompt: Scene & Mood: Sharp studio editorial built around a single continuous spin transformation. A woman in a fitted matte-black slip dress stands center frame under moody spotlighting, still and composed, then spins once and completes the rotation in a completely different look: a structured chrome art-deco gown with metallic panel detailing. The mood is theatrical, high-impact, confident, with the spin treated as one unbroken magic trick rather than a cut. Frame Map: Begin in a medium-full frontal composition, subject centered, arms relaxed at her sides, dark studio backdrop with a single hard key light from camera-left casting a long diagonal shadow. Maintain headroom above and enough negative space on both sides to track the dress silhouette expanding mid-spin. The floor is glossy black, reflecting a faint silhouette. Subject Lock: Keep the same face, hair part, height, and body proportions throughout both looks. Look A: sleek middle-parted dark hair, matte-black slip dress, bare shoulders, minimal silver jewelry, neutral confident expression. Look B (post-spin): same hair now swept into a sharp low chignon, structured chrome-panel gown with a stiff architectural collar, metallic cuff on one wrist, same facial features and expression carried through. Do not change her height, face shape, or skin tone between looks. Cross-Frame Rules: She is the only person and subject in frame at all times. The transformation must occur entirely within the single continuous spin motion — no jump cuts, no freeze frames, no duplicated bodies mid-spin. Fabric physics must look weighty and real during the whirl, not liquid or melting. No on-screen text, no captions, no signage typography, no rendered text in the frame. Movement: 6 seconds total. She begins still for 1 second, then initiates a fast single clockwise spin over 2 seconds, dress and hair flaring outward with real centrifugal motion, arms lifting slightly for balance. As she completes the rotation and faces camera again, the new gown settles into place with a final fabric snap and hair falls into its chignon shape naturally. She holds the new pose, still and composed, for the final 3 seconds, chin lifted, eyes locked on camera. Last Frame: She stands still in the chrome art-deco gown, facing camera directly, chin slightly lifted, one hand resting at her hip, expression calm and powerful. Studio light holds steady on her face. No on-screen text, no captions, no signage typography, no rendered text in the frame. World Plate: Minimal black-box studio, single hard key light, glossy reflective floor, deep shadow falloff into the background with no visible walls or props. Clean, high-contrast, editorial darkness. Sound Bed: Diegetic audio only: fabric whoosh during the spin, a soft heel pivot on the glossy floor, faint jewelry chime, quiet room tone. No music, no soundtrack, no score, no lyrics. Capture Realism: Natural skin texture, real fabric weight and flare physics, believable hair movement settling into the chignon, grounded contact shadows, soft highlight rolloff, fine 35mm grain. Avoid AI gloss, warped limbs, melted fabric, duplicated body parts, or hair clipping through the gown collar. Camera Capture: 6 seconds, 24fps, locked-off static camera, 50mm lens, shallow depth of field isolating subject from the dark backdrop, punchy contrast grade, fine grain, crisp studio realism.

items.prompt: THIS GUY CONNECTED FABLE 5 + HIGGSFIELD SO ONE CLAUDE PROMPT CAN BECOME 5 DIFFERENT CREATIVE ASSETS The interesting part is not “Claude can make a video.” It is the stack shape. Claude becomes the front door. Fable 5 handles the creative brief/control layer. Higgsfield gives the workflow access to image and video generation. Then one prompt can branch into different outputs instead of dying as one static answer. The video shows the simple version: Open Claude. Add a custom connector. Paste the Higgsfield MCP connector back in. Use Claude to drive the creative stack. The demos are the scroll-stopper: realistic UGC-style ad creatives animated websites 3D models turned into cinematic scenes years of research turned into an interactive game world scripts turned into explainer videos with generated visuals That is the specific payoff. A solo marketer can test 5 ad directions before hiring a production team. A founder can turn a landing page idea into motion assets in the same session. A creator can move from script to visual treatment without manually opening 6 different tools. The reusable mechanism is simple: the brief, the routing, and the asset generation start happening inside one conversation. That changes who can prototype. Not because every output is production-ready. Because the first version gets cheaper, faster, and more visual. Caveat is obvious: this is still a connector workflow, not magic production quality. You still need taste, prompting, iteration, rights checks, and a human deciding what is usable. But Fable 5 + Higgsfield is one of the clearest examples of where Claude is going: less chatbot, more creative software control room.

items.prompt: 2.8 million views. Without a single real ingredient. No stove. No camera. No chef. While most people spend hours filming, buying ingredients, and chasing perfect lighting, someone else is already getting millions of views from content that never existed in the real world. And if you ignore this trend today, in just a few years you may find yourself watching others profit from the new attention economy while you’re trying to catch up. The secret lies in disciplined prompt engineering. You don’t ask AI to simply “make a video.” You first generate a photorealistic reference image of the dish, then break it into 10 separate scenes with precisely defined camera angles, motion blur, depth of field, rising steam, and the tiny visual details that convince viewers they’re watching a real kitchen. Each scene is turned into a two-second clip using Image-to-Video generators, then everything is assembled in CapCut with trending music and automatic captions. Those captions - combined with the right editing pace - are crucial for audience retention because today’s viewers want to watch food that looks irresistible, whether it exists in the real world or not. Instead of being limited by filming, expensive equipment, or lighting, you become the architect of a content factory that can scale almost infinitely - from earning through Creator Rewards to selling AI-generated food content to restaurants that want flawless videos without renting a studio or hiring professional chefs. This isn’t the future anymore - it’s the new attention economy. And in this economy, your greatest asset isn’t culinary talent. It’s your ability to write prompts that make the TikTok, Facebook, and YouTube algorithms work for you. While others are cooking meals, you can build a scalable system, hit “Export,” and collect views that turn into real income.

items.prompt: 🚨GUESS WHICH VIDEO WAS SHOT ON A REAL CAMERA AND WHICH ONE WAS MADE IN SEEDANCE To make AI video look real, it’s not enough to just write “realistic”. You have to deliberately add the things that usually ruin a shot: > Shaky handheld camera > Slight digital artifacts > Small focus misses These “imperfections” are exactly what makes it feel alive. SHOT 9 (27–30s) — THE PERFECT MOMENT Romantic montage: • Riding the toy Ferris wheel • Sharing oversized cotton candy • Playing carnival games • Taking a selfie under glowing lights Final hero frame: Both toys hold hands beneath the Ferris wheel. items.prompt: 📖SEEDANCE 2.5 VS 2.0: THE FIRST AI VIDEO MODEL THAT DOESN'T FORCE YOU TO STITCH CLIPS TOGETHER. ByteDance skipped straight from 2.0 to 2.5 — no small update, a generational jump. Seedance 2.0 caps out at 15 seconds per clip. Anything longer means generating multiple pieces and stitching them on a timeline, hoping the face, lighting, and motion hold up across the cut. items.prompt: 28-th Prompt for AI model Scene 1: Seedance 2.0 | 10 seconds | Ultra-realistic live-action cinematic | Single continuous take | Absolutely NO CUTS | TRUE IMAX cinematic presentation | 24fps | Wild organic handheld cinematography | Raw documentary realism | Deliberately imperfect framing | Subject frequently off-center | Aggressive whip pans | Violent push-ins | Natural operator corrections | Fight choreography inspired by Atomic Blonde | Color grading inspired by Atomic Blonde with subtle Gothic noir: cold steel-blue shadows, warm golden chandelier highlights, rich burgundy tones, deep blacks, high contrast, subtle film grain. ABSOLUTELY NO MUSIC. Only realistic production audio: polished marble footsteps, breathing, cloth movement, leather coat movement, heavy body impacts, punches, elbows, knees, kicks, subtle bone impacts, marble echoes, broken crystal, drifting debris, natural ballroom ambience. MAIN SUBJECT Man identical to the uploaded reference image. Identical face, hairstyle, facial hair, skin tone, body proportions, tattoos, expression, and outfit. Wearing the identical luxurious white tailored suit with the jacket open, exposing the chest tattoos, white tailored trousers, black belt with a large gold “M” buckle, gold waist chain, white sneakers, dark sunglasses, wristwatch, and the identical dramatic long black feather coat draped over his shoulders. Hair tied into the identical man bun throughout the sequence. Calm, fearless, emotionless, highly trained elite assassin. LOCATION A breathtaking Gothic European grand ballroom inside an ancient luxury palace. Towering black marble columns. Massive crystal chandeliers. Gothic vaulted ceiling. Pointed arches. Black-and-gold baroque architecture. Tall stained-glass windows. Polished black-and-white marble floor reflecting warm chandelier light. Thin atmospheric haze. Completely empty. No furniture. No tables. No chairs. No guests. Only the man and three elite villains. VILLAINS Three elite professional fighters wearing impeccably tailored black Italian suits, crisp white dress shirts, black ties, and polished black leather shoes. Athletic, disciplined, intimidating, fighting with ruthless efficiency using realistic close-quarters combat. CAMERA LANGUAGE The camera behaves like a real combat cameraman trapped inside the fight. Wild handheld movement. Violent whip pans. Rapid push-ins. Micro-shakes. Sudden reframing. Realistic focus breathing. Natural rolling shutter. Bodies repeatedly block the lens. The operator almost loses the subject multiple times before instinctively recovering. The man is intentionally not centered for much of the sequence. TIMELINE 0.0–1.5s The handheld camera follows closely behind the man as he walks confidently along the second-floor balcony overlooking the vast Gothic ballroom. Without hesitation, he plants one foot onto the marble railing and launches himself into the enormous open atrium. His long black feather coat billows dramatically behind him. The camera instinctively dives after him, briefly losing the frame. 1.5–2.8s Falling beside him beneath the enormous crystal chandeliers, the camera struggles to keep pace. His feather coat and open white suit move naturally through the air before he rotates smoothly and lands in a powerful three-point landing. Marble dust and tiny crystal fragments burst across the polished floor. 2.8–3.8s Three elite villains slowly emerge from different directions, silently surrounding him in a loose triangle formation. They immediately rush forward together. 3.8–6.2s The fight erupts instantly. He slips between the first two attackers with explosive footwork, smashing a brutal elbow into the first villain’s jaw before driving a crushing knee into the second villain’s ribs. The handheld camera violently whip-pans between impacts, repeatedly blocked by moving bodies before recovering the action. Light blood sprays from a split lip. No gore. #actionmovie #fight

items.prompt: I used to do a lot of these mini city prompts. Here is a new structure I have been trying lately. Animated with Kling. Prompt: I(0) = empty palm of hand, no sphere. I(1) = full detailed micro‑globe. ∂I/∂t = Δ(I, $ CITY) guided by: - Sphere appearing in palm. - Skyline crust growing radially as tiny plastic blocks. - Artery wrapping and curving. - Life details popping in. - Lighting evolving to daylight, DOF engaging. Integration: t=0.0–0.2: Hand appears, empty sphere materializes as a smooth grey ball. t=0.2–0.5: Building blocks erupt from surface, filling all space, height map guided by $ CITY. t=0.5–0.7: Artery curves around the front, dividing the dense crust. t=0.7–0.9: Tiny cars, boats, trees appear; material shifts to architectural model (plastic/wood). t=0.9–1.0: Daylight and DOF finalize, foreground hand sharp, background bokeh. Output I(1): photorealistic 1:1 macro image, ultra‑detailed, no empty space.

She runs across wet steel beams and exposed concrete toward the outer edge of the construction site while security chases behind her. A giant crane towers overhead, its heavy hook and cable swinging violently in the wind between this tower and a second unfinished skyscraper nearby. Rain lashes the structure, warning lights blink red, and the city glows far below through mist. Side shot: the agent grabs the swinging crane hook or cable and is pulled out into open air between the two skyscrapers. She crashes feet-first into the outer framework, struggles for a split second to hold on, then pulls herself onto a narrow beam or platform. The crane hook swings away behind her as she regains balance and keeps moving forward. Final moment: the female agent lands on the second skyscraper structure and turns briefly as the crane continues swinging behind her in the storm, with the neon skyline far below. items.prompt: Between Friday and Saturday, another prompt is dropped: Tha Dam - Seedance 2.0 on @Hailuo_AI Hyper-realistic cinematic action sequence, 15 seconds, aspect ratio 16:9. Daytime during a violent storm. Two agents, one man and one woman, run along the top of a massive concrete dam while a security team chases behind them. The dam is huge and exposed, with narrow maintenance walkways, steel railings, warning lights, control boxes, heavy spray, and roaring water far below. Dark clouds gather overhead, wind drives rain across the structure, and the entire dam feels unstable under growing pressure. Wide opening shot: the two agents sprint along the top of the dam at full speed while security appears behind them, closing in. Water crashes below on one side, and storm wind pushes mist and spray across the walkway. Tracking shot: the agents keep running along the narrow concrete path as warning alarms flash. Ahead, massive spillway gates begin opening one by one. The structure shudders under the force, water erupts downward in huge torrents, and the agents struggle to keep balance on the slick surface. Side shot: the pressure increases. The dam shakes harder as more gates open. Spray blasts across the walkway, metal railings rattle, and one section of the path cracks near the edge. The agents keep moving, ducking around control structures and staying ahead of the security team. Final 5 seconds: the action becomes extreme. A maintenance section ahead partially breaks and drops, creating a gap in the walkway. The agents accelerate into a final desperate sprint, leap across the broken section, land hard, and keep moving while the spillway fully opens beside them. Water explodes downward with enormous force, the whole structure trembles, and the security team is slowed behind by spray and collapsing debris. Final moment: the two agents reach a safer platform near a control access door while the open spillway roars beside them, with storm, mist, and massive water pressure filling the frame.
